notes:
1. Thanthai Periyar — Overview

  • Erode Venkata Ramasamy was a major social reformer, rationalist and leader of the non-Brahmin and Dravidian movements in Tamil Nadu.
  • He fought against:
  • Untouchability.
  • Caste hierarchy.
  • Social inequality.
  • Gender discrimination.
  • Religious superstition.
  • He founded the Self-Respect Movement.
  • He later transformed the Justice Party into the Dravidar Kazhagam.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Self-Respect Movement + Rationalism + Social Justice + Dravidar Kazhagam

2. Full Name

  • His full name was Erode Venkata Ramasamy.
  • He is generally referred to as E.V. Ramasamy or E.V.R.
📌 Must-Memorise

E.V.R. → Erode Venkata Ramasamy

3. Popular Title

  • He became universally known as Periyar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → E.V. Ramasamy

4. Meaning of Periyar

  • The Tamil word Periyar means "Great Person" or "Great One."

5. Thanthai Periyar

  • He is also popularly called Thanthai Periyar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Thanthai Periyar → E.V. Ramasamy

6. Birth

  • Periyar was born on 17 September 1879.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → 17 September 1879

7. Birthplace

  • He was born at Erode in present-day Tamil Nadu.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Erode

8. Father

  • His father was Venkatappa Naicker.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar's Father → Venkatappa Naicker

9. Mother

  • His mother was Chinnathayammal.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar's Mother → Chinnathayammal

10. Family Background

  • Periyar was born into a prosperous trading family.
  • His family was involved in commerce at Erode.

11. Formal Schooling

  • Periyar received only limited formal schooling.
  • He later developed his ideas largely through:
  • Experience.
  • Reading.
  • Political activity.
  • Public debate.

12. Business Career

  • Before becoming a full-time political and social activist, Periyar participated in the family's business activities.

13. Public Service at Erode

  • Periyar became active in local civic affairs.
  • He held positions connected with Erode municipal administration.

14. Chairman of Erode Municipality

  • Periyar served as Chairman of the Erode Municipality.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Periyar → Erode Municipal Administration

15. Municipal Work

His civic work included attention to:

  • Sanitation.
  • Public health.
  • Water supply.
  • Local administration.

16. Social Service

  • Periyar was involved in public-service activities before becoming a major ideological leader.

17. Personal Experience of Caste

  • Experiences of caste discrimination deeply shaped his later opposition to caste hierarchy.

18. Kasi Experience

  • Periyar's journey to Kasi, or Varanasi, became important in accounts of his intellectual development.
  • He encountered discrimination and practices that reinforced his criticism of caste and religious orthodoxy.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Kasi Experience → Strengthened Periyar's Anti-Caste Criticism

19. Critique of Religious Orthodoxy

  • Periyar increasingly argued that religious authority often legitimised social inequality.

20. Entry into Congress

  • Periyar joined the Indian National Congress during the Gandhian phase of the national movement.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Congress Before Self-Respect Movement

21. Gandhian Influence

During his Congress years, Periyar supported:

  • Non-Cooperation.
  • Khadi.
  • Prohibition.
  • Removal of untouchability.

22. Non-Cooperation Movement

  • Periyar actively participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement of the early 1920s.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Non-Cooperation Movement

23. Khadi

  • He promoted khadi as part of the Congress constructive programme.

24. Foreign Cloth Boycott

  • Periyar supported the boycott of foreign goods and colonial institutions.

25. Prohibition

  • Prohibition was one of the causes Periyar strongly supported during his Congress phase.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Strong Advocate of Prohibition

26. Toddy-Shop Picketing

  • Periyar participated in campaigns against liquor shops.
  • Members of his family also took part in prohibition-related agitation.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Periyar → Toddy-Shop Picketing

27. Nagammai

  • Periyar's first wife was Nagammai.
  • She became an important participant in his social and political activities.
📌 Must-Memorise

Nagammai → Periyar's Wife + Activist

28. Women in Agitation

  • Nagammai and other women participated in:
  • Prohibition campaigns.
  • Social reform.
  • Self-Respect activities.

29. Periyar and Congress Organisation

  • Periyar became an important Congress leader in the Madras Presidency.

30. Tamil Nadu Congress

  • He held organisational responsibilities within the Tamil Nadu Congress movement.

31. Social Equality Within Congress

  • Periyar increasingly demanded that Congress address caste inequality alongside political independence.

32. Communal Representation

  • One of Periyar's major demands was communal representation in:
  • Education.
  • Government employment.
  • Political institutions.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Communal Representation / Social Justice

33. Meaning of Communal Representation

  • In the political vocabulary of the Madras Presidency, communal representation referred to allocation of opportunities among social communities to prevent domination by a small section.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

"Communal" Here → Representation by Social Communities

Not Simply Religious Communalism

34. Periyar's Argument

  • Periyar argued that formal equality alone could not correct deeply unequal access to:
  • Education.
  • Government jobs.
  • Political power.

35. Congress Disagreement

  • Congress did not accept Periyar's demands for communal representation in the manner he wanted.

36. Cheranmahadevi Gurukulam

  • The Cheranmahadevi Gurukulam controversy became an important turning point in Periyar's relationship with Congress.
📌 Must-Memorise

Cheranmahadevi Gurukulam → Periyar → Caste Equality Issue

37. V.V.S. Aiyar

  • The Gurukulam was associated with nationalist V.V.S. Aiyar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Cheranmahadevi Gurukulam → V.V.S. Aiyar

38. Gurukulam Issue

  • Allegations of caste-based segregation in dining and treatment led to major controversy.

39. Periyar's Objection

  • Periyar strongly criticised caste discrimination within an institution supported by nationalist funds.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Political Nationalism Without Social Equality → Rejected by Periyar

40. Significance of Gurukulam Controversy

  • The dispute strengthened Periyar's belief that ending British rule alone would not automatically destroy caste inequality.

41. Vaikom Satyagraha

  • The Vaikom Satyagraha took place in Travancore during 1924–25.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vaikom Satyagraha → 1924–25

42. Location

  • Vaikom is in present-day Kerala.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Vaikom → Kerala, Not Tamil Nadu

43. Issue at Vaikom

  • Members of oppressed communities were restricted from using certain roads surrounding the Vaikom temple.

44. Purpose

The movement demanded:

  • Equal access to public roads.
  • Removal of caste-based restrictions.

45. Periyar at Vaikom

  • Periyar travelled to Vaikom and participated actively in the agitation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Vaikom Satyagraha

46. Arrest at Vaikom

  • Periyar was arrested and imprisoned for his participation in the movement.

47. Vaikom Veerar

  • His role in the agitation earned him the popular title Vaikom Veerar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Vaikom Veerar → Periyar

48. Vaikom Hero Title

  • "Vaikom Veerar" means Hero of Vaikom.

49. Gandhi at Vaikom

  • Gandhi later visited Vaikom and participated in negotiations.
  • Gandhi and Periyar approached caste reform differently.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Vaikom → Both Gandhi and Periyar Associated, But in Different Roles

50. Vaikom Significance

  • Vaikom strengthened Periyar's identification with struggles for:
  • Social equality.
  • Public access.
  • Anti-untouchability.

51. Leaving Congress

  • Periyar left the Indian National Congress in 1925.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar Left Congress → 1925

52. Reasons for Leaving Congress

Major reasons included his dissatisfaction over:

  • Caste inequality.
  • Communal representation.
  • Social reform priorities.
  • Congress's response to the Gurukulam controversy.

53. Political Freedom vs Social Freedom

  • Periyar argued that Swaraj without social equality could preserve domination by privileged social groups.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Social Liberation Before/Alongside Political Liberation

54. Self-Respect Movement

  • Periyar launched the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.
📌 Must-Memorise

Self-Respect Movement → 1925 → Periyar

55. Tamil Name

  • The movement became known in Tamil as the Suya Mariyathai Iyakkam.
📌 Must-Memorise

Suya Mariyathai Iyakkam → Self-Respect Movement

56. Main Aim

  • Its central objective was to create a society based on:
  • Dignity.
  • Equality.
  • Rationalism.
  • Freedom from caste domination.

57. Meaning of Self-Respect

For Periyar, self-respect meant that no person should accept inferiority based on:

  • Caste.
  • Birth.
  • Gender.
  • Religion.

58. Anti-Caste Principle

  • Destruction of caste hierarchy became the movement's central social objective.
📌 Must-Memorise

Self-Respect Movement → Anti-Caste

59. Rationalism

  • The movement encouraged people to examine traditions using reason rather than unquestioned faith.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Rationalism

60. Superstition

  • Periyar criticised practices he regarded as:
  • Superstitious.
  • Irrational.
  • Socially oppressive.

61. Religious Authority

  • He rejected the claim that religious scriptures or priests should determine social status.

62. Brahminism

  • Periyar's writings frequently attacked "Brahminism."
  • By this, he primarily meant the ideological system of caste hierarchy and priestly domination.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Periyar's Critique of Brahminism → Ideological/Social Hierarchy

Do Not Reduce It to a Simple Personal Dispute

63. Varna System

  • Periyar strongly rejected the four-fold varna hierarchy.

64. Untouchability

  • He regarded untouchability as one of the most extreme consequences of caste.

65. Birth-Based Status

  • Periyar rejected all claims that occupation or social dignity should be determined by birth.

66. Social Equality

  • He demanded equal human dignity irrespective of caste origin.

67. Self-Respect Conferences

  • Self-Respect conferences became important platforms for spreading:
  • Rationalism.
  • Anti-caste ideas.
  • Women's rights.
  • Social reform.

68. Chengalpattu Conference

  • The first major provincial Self-Respect Conference was held at Chengalpattu in 1929.
📌 Must-Memorise

Self-Respect Conference → Chengalpattu → 1929

69. Conference Resolutions

Self-Respect conferences discussed:

  • Caste abolition.
  • Women's rights.
  • Marriage reform.
  • Property rights.
  • Religious reform.

70. Self-Respect Marriage

  • Self-Respect marriages rejected the requirement of Brahmin priests and Sanskrit rituals.
📌 Must-Memorise

Self-Respect Marriage → No Priest-Centred Ritual Requirement

71. Marriage as Contract

  • Periyar regarded marriage as a partnership between equals rather than a sacramental relationship based on female subordination.

72. Inter-Caste Marriage

  • The movement encouraged inter-caste marriage as a means of weakening caste boundaries.

73. Widow Remarriage

  • Periyar strongly supported widow remarriage.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Widow Remarriage

74. Women's Choice in Marriage

  • He argued that women must have freedom in choosing their marriage partners.

75. Divorce

  • Periyar supported the right to divorce when a marriage became oppressive or incompatible.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Self-Respect Movement → Women's Right to Divorce

76. Women's Property Rights

  • He advocated equal property and inheritance rights for women.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Women's Property Rights

77. Female Education

  • Periyar considered women's education essential for social liberation.

78. Child Marriage

  • He strongly opposed child marriage.

79. Women's Employment

  • Periyar supported women's participation in employment and public life.

80. Patriarchy

  • He criticised patriarchal customs that treated women as dependent on men.

81. Motherhood and Choice

  • Periyar argued that women should possess greater control over decisions concerning childbirth and family life.

82. Gender Equality

  • Women's liberation was not a secondary issue in Periyar's ideology.
  • It formed a core part of his concept of social equality.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Radical Advocate of Women's Equality

83. Nagammai's Role

  • Nagammai helped organise women within the Self-Respect movement.

84. Kannammal

  • Periyar's sister Kannammal also participated in social-reform and political activities.
🔗 Tamil Nadu Key Link

Periyar's Family → Women Active in Reform Politics

85. Kudi Arasu

  • Periyar started the Tamil weekly Kudi Arasu in 1925.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kudi Arasu → 1925 → Periyar

86. Meaning of Kudi Arasu

  • Kudi Arasu means "Republic" or broadly "People's Rule."

87. Purpose of Kudi Arasu

It became a major platform for:

  • Self-Respect ideology.
  • Rationalism.
  • Anti-caste criticism.
  • Women's emancipation.

88. Publication Language

  • Kudi Arasu was published in Tamil.
📌 Must-Memorise

Kudi Arasu → Tamil

89. Revolt

  • Periyar also used an English-language publication called Revolt to spread Self-Respect ideas more widely.
📌 Must-Memorise

Revolt → English Publication Associated with Periyar

90. Puratchi

  • Puratchi was another publication associated with Periyar's movement.

91. Pagutharivu

  • Pagutharivu, meaning rationalism or rational thought, was another important publication associated with his ideological work.
📌 Must-Memorise

Pagutharivu → Rationalism

92. Viduthalai

  • Viduthalai became the most enduring newspaper associated with Periyar and the Dravidian movement.
📌 Must-Memorise

Viduthalai → Periyar / Dravidar Kazhagam

93. Journalism as Movement Tool

  • Periyar relied heavily on print media to challenge social conventions and communicate with ordinary people.

94. Public Speaking

  • His speeches were:
  • Direct.
  • Provocative.
  • Designed to challenge inherited authority.

95. Tamil Language

  • Periyar used Tamil extensively as the language of mass political communication.

96. Language and Social Equality

  • He opposed the use of language as a means of cultural domination.

97. Anti-Hindi Movement — Background

  • C. Rajagopalachari became Premier of Madras Presidency in 1937.

98. Compulsory Hindi

  • Rajaji's government introduced compulsory Hindi teaching in selected schools.
📌 Must-Memorise

Compulsory Hindi → Rajaji Ministry

99. Periyar's Opposition

  • Periyar became one of the strongest leaders of the anti-Hindi agitation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Anti-Hindi Agitation → Periyar

100. First Anti-Hindi Agitation

  • The major agitation began in 1937–38.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Anti-Hindi Agitation → 1937–40 Period

101. Why Periyar Opposed Compulsory Hindi

He argued that compulsory Hindi:

  • Threatened Tamil.
  • Imposed cultural domination.
  • Created unequal advantages.
  • Reduced linguistic freedom.

102. Tamil Identity

  • Anti-Hindi agitation strengthened the relationship between:
  • Language.
  • Social justice.
  • Tamil political identity.

103. Protest Methods

The movement used:

  • Demonstrations.
  • Public meetings.
  • Picketing.
  • Publications.
  • Civil disobedience.

104. Arrest

  • Periyar was arrested during the anti-Hindi agitation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Imprisoned in Anti-Hindi Movement

105. Thalamuthu

  • Natarajan and Thalamuthu became remembered as martyrs associated with the anti-Hindi agitation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Thalamuthu + Natarajan → Anti-Hindi Agitation

106. Language Martyrs

  • Their deaths became powerful symbols in Tamil language politics.

107. End of Compulsory Hindi

  • The compulsory Hindi policy was eventually withdrawn after the Congress ministry resigned and the political situation changed.

108. Periyar's Language Position

  • He opposed forced linguistic uniformity.
  • His position emphasised:
  • Tamil rights.
  • Regional linguistic autonomy.

109. English

  • Periyar sometimes supported the continued use of English as a neutral or practical link language rather than compulsory Hindi dominance.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Periyar → Anti-Hindi, Not Anti-Language Learning in General

110. Justice Party

  • The Justice Party had been founded in 1916 by leaders of the non-Brahmin political movement.
📌 Must-Memorise

Justice Party → 1916

111. Justice Party Background

The party sought:

  • Non-Brahmin representation.
  • Educational opportunity.
  • Government employment.
  • Communal representation.

112. South Indian Liberal Federation

  • The Justice Party's formal organisational name was the South Indian Liberal Federation.
📌 Must-Memorise

South Indian Liberal Federation → Justice Party

113. Periyar and Justice Party

  • During the 1930s, Periyar's Self-Respect Movement and Justice Party increasingly converged politically.

114. Leadership of Justice Party

  • Periyar became the leader/president of the Justice Party in the late 1930s.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Justice Party Leadership

115. Justice Party Transformation

  • Under Periyar, the Justice Party became increasingly:
  • Social-reform oriented.
  • Rationalist.
  • Dravidian in ideological character.

116. Electoral Politics

  • Periyar gradually moved away from the pursuit of government office through electoral politics.

117. Social Revolution First

  • He believed social transformation was more important than simply capturing political office.

118. Dravidian Identity

  • Periyar developed a political language centred on Dravidian social and cultural identity.

119. Dravidar

  • "Dravidar" became a political-social identity used to challenge caste hierarchy and northern cultural domination.

120. Dravida Nadu

  • Periyar at various stages advocated a separate Dravidian political unit, often referred to as Dravida Nadu.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Periyar → Dravida Nadu Demand

121. Context of Dravida Nadu Demand

The demand reflected opposition to:

  • Caste domination.
  • Centralised cultural nationalism.
  • Hindi imposition.
  • Perceived northern political domination.

122. Justice Party Conference — Salem

  • In 1944, the Justice Party was transformed into the Dravidar Kazhagam at the Salem conference.
📌 Must-Memorise

Justice Party → Dravidar Kazhagam → 1944 → Salem

123. Dravidar Kazhagam

  • Dravidar Kazhagam is commonly abbreviated as DK.
📌 Must-Memorise

DK → Dravidar Kazhagam

124. Periyar as DK Leader

  • Periyar became the ideological and organisational leader of Dravidar Kazhagam.

125. DK and Elections

  • Dravidar Kazhagam did not primarily seek participation in electoral politics.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

DK → Social Movement, Not Electoral Party

126. DK Programme

It promoted:

  • Rationalism.
  • Self-respect.
  • Caste abolition.
  • Women's rights.
  • Dravidian identity.
  • Opposition to Hindi imposition.

127. Black Shirt Movement

  • Black shirts became a visible symbol associated with the Dravidian movement under Periyar.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Black Shirt → Periyar / Dravidar Kazhagam

128. Symbolism of Black

  • Black symbolised protest against:
  • Social oppression.
  • Inequality.
  • Humiliation.

129. Independence — 1947

  • India became independent on 15 August 1947.

130. Periyar's View of Independence

  • Periyar was critical of celebrating political independence as complete liberation.
  • He argued that caste and social inequalities remained.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

Periyar's Position → Political Independence Did Not Equal Social Liberation

131. Social Freedom

  • For Periyar, genuine freedom required:
  • Destruction of caste hierarchy.
  • Women's emancipation.
  • Rationalism.
  • Equal representation.

132. Indian Constitution

  • Periyar later criticised constitutional and social arrangements that he believed failed to eliminate caste hierarchy sufficiently.

133. Reservation

  • Periyar strongly supported reservation and communal representation as mechanisms of social justice.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Reservation / Communal Representation

134. Communal G.O. Context

  • Communal reservation in the Madras Presidency developed before independence under Justice Party governments.
  • Periyar strongly defended the principle.

135. Champakam Dorairajan Case

  • The Supreme Court's decision in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan in 1951 affected the communal reservation system.
📌 Must-Memorise

Champakam Dorairajan Case → 1951 → Reservation Context

136. Social Reaction

  • The judgment produced strong political mobilisation in Madras State in defence of reservation and social justice.

137. First Constitutional Amendment

  • Parliament enacted the First Constitutional Amendment in 1951.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Constitutional Amendment → 1951

138. Article 15(4)

  • The constitutional framework was changed to enable special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Social Justice Mobilisation → First Amendment Context → Article 15(4)

139. Periyar's Role

  • Periyar's movement was one of the strongest social forces in Madras demanding protection of communal reservation.

140. Social Justice Legacy

  • Reservation policy later became one of the defining features of Tamil Nadu's political system.

141. DK–DMK Split

  • A major split occurred within the Dravidian movement in 1949.
📌 Must-Memorise

DMK Founded → 1949

142. C.N. Annadurai

  • C.N. Annadurai had been an important follower and colleague of Periyar.
📌 Must-Memorise

Anna → Initially Associated with Periyar's DK

143. Maniammai Marriage

  • Periyar's marriage to Maniammai in 1949 became one factor contributing to internal disputes within the movement.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

1949 → Periyar–Maniammai Marriage + DK Internal Crisis

144. Deeper Political Difference

  • The split was not caused solely by the marriage.
  • Differences also existed over:
  • Electoral politics.
  • Political strategy.
  • Leadership.
  • Timing of social and political change.
⚠️ TNPSC Caution

DK–DMK Split → Multiple Causes

145. Formation of DMK

  • C.N. Annadurai and his supporters founded the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam in 1949.
📌 Must-Memorise

DMK → 1949 → C.N. Annadurai

146. DK vs DMK

Dravidar Kazhagam:

  • Periyar.
  • Social reform movement.
  • Avoided electoral politics.

DMK:

  • Annadurai.
  • Participated in electoral politics.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Trap

DK → Periyar

DMK → Anna

147. Relationship After Split

  • Periyar and Annadurai differed politically but continued to share several broad social-reform goals.

148. Anti-Hindi Politics After Independence

  • Periyar continued to oppose attempts to make Hindi dominant in administration and education.

149. Official Language Issue

  • The approaching constitutional transition regarding official-language policy intensified anti-Hindi mobilisation in Tamil Nadu.

150. 1965 Anti-Hindi Agitation

  • Large-scale anti-Hindi agitations erupted in Tamil Nadu in 1965.
📌 Must-Memorise

Major Anti-Hindi Agitation → 1965

151. Periyar and 1965

  • Periyar remained an important ideological figure in the wider anti-Hindi political environment.
  • Student and party mobilisation, however, had developed beyond the original Self-Respect organisational structure.

152. DMK and Anti-Hindi Politics

  • The DMK became one of the principal political beneficiaries of anti-Hindi sentiment.

153. 1967 Political Change

  • DMK defeated Congress in Madras State in 1967.
📌 Must-Memorise

1967 → DMK Government

154. Annadurai

  • C.N. Annadurai became Chief Minister in 1967.

155. Periyar and DMK Government

  • The rise of the DMK represented the electoral triumph of a political tradition that had roots in the Self-Respect and Dravidian movements.

156. Self-Respect Marriage — Legal Recognition

  • The DMK government gave legal recognition to Self-Respect marriages in Tamil Nadu through state legislation.
📌 Tamil Nadu Must-Memorise

Self-Respect Marriage Legal Recognition → DMK Government / Annadurai Era

157. Significance

  • Legal recognition institutionalised one of Periyar's most important social-reform practices.

158. Tamil Nadu Name

  • Madras State was renamed Tamil Nadu in 1969.
📌 Must-Memorise

Madras State → Tamil Nadu → 1969

159. Periyar and Tamil Identity

  • Periyar's movement played a major role in strengthening Tamil linguistic and regional consciousness.

160. Tamil Nationalism — Caution

  • Periyar's Dravidian politics should not be reduced simply to literary Tamil nationalism.
  • His central concern remained social hierarchy and rationalist reform.

161. Tamil Script Reform

  • Periyar advocated simplification and reform of the Tamil script.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Tamil Script Reform

162. Purpose of Script Reform

  • He believed simplified writing could make:
  • Printing.
  • Education.
  • Literacy.

more accessible.

163. Tamil and Rationalism

  • Periyar valued Tamil while also criticising traditions within Tamil society that supported caste and superstition.
🔗 TNPSC Key Link

Periyar → Tamil Pride + Criticism of Oppressive Tamil Traditions

164. Ancient Literature — Critical Approach

  • He did not believe that every ancient text should be accepted merely because it was old or Tamil.

165. Ramayana Criticism

  • Periyar strongly criticised the Ramayana and its social-cultural interpretations.

166. Mythological Critique

  • He used criticism of mythology to challenge:
  • Caste ideology.
  • Patriarchy.
  • Cultural domination.

167. Religious Iconoclasm

  • Periyar sometimes used provocative symbolic actions to question religious authority and inherited belief.

168. Rationalist Method

His central demand was:

  • Ask why.
  • Examine evidence.
  • Reject blind obedience.

169. Atheism

  • Periyar openly identified with atheistic and rationalist criticism of organised religion.
📌 Must-Memorise

Periyar → Rationalism + Atheism

170. Humanism

  • His social philosophy placed human dignity above divine or scriptural authority.

171. "No God" Slogans

  • Periyar used strongly anti-religious slogans as instruments of rationalist propaganda.

172. Aim of Religious Criticism

  • His attacks on religion were primarily connected with his opposition to institutions and beliefs that he believed sustained inequality.

173. Caste Titles

  • Periyar encouraged people to stop using caste-identifying titles and symbols.
📌 Must-Memorise

Self-Respect → Reject Caste Markers

174. Dining Equality

  • Inter-dining among castes was encouraged to weaken notions of ritual purity.

175. Inter-Caste Marriage

  • Inter-caste marriage was treated as a practical attack on caste reproduction.

176. Temple Entry

  • Periyar supported equal public access but increasingly questioned the institution of religion itself.

177. Temple Entry vs Rationalism

  • His movement went beyond demanding entry into temples.
  • It also asked why caste and priestly institutions should possess social authority.

178. Gandhi and Periyar — Similarity

Both opposed:

  • Untouchability.
  • Social exclusion.

179. Gandhi and Periyar — Difference

Gandhi:

  • Sought reform within a religious-moral framework.

Periyar:

  • Rejected caste ideology and religious authority more fundamentally.
⚠️ TNPSC Favourite Comparison

Gandhi → Reformist Religious Framework

Periyar → Rationalist Anti-Caste Framework

180. Ambedkar and Periyar

  • B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar shared strong opposition to:
  • Caste hierarchy.
  • Untouchability.
  • Birth-based inequality.

181. Differences with Ambedkar

  • Their organisations, political methods and constitutional strategies differed.
  • Ambedkar relied heavily on:
  • Law.
  • Constitutional safeguards.
